description: Deep violet scattered with white specks, dropped by a Duskhoof. Like it, the stone casts no shadow.
lore: Put one on a windowsill in the sun. Everything else on that sill lays a shadow; beside this there is a clean bright place where a shadow should be and is not, and it will go on doing that all day, on any sill, for anybody who cares to stand and watch it. That is what makes the thing worth a hundred and fifty gold, and something else besides. It is not a story about an animal at dusk in poor light told by a man who has had a drink. It is a stone on a plank, and it holds.

On a person it works the way it works on the light. Stand still in shadow with one on you and you are not hidden so much as declined: eyes arrive, then find somewhere else to be, then go back to whatever they were doing. Moving in the dark, hands miss. Sellers state this plainly and buyers ask twice anyway, because it does not sound like a thing a stone should be able to do to a person.

[[characters/646b922c|Sigrun]] sets stones into steel for a living, and there is one she hands back. She takes it out of the cloth, looks at it as long as anybody does, and says she has enough work on. There is a black horse in her yard that hauls charcoal and leans its whole weight into her hand of an evening; every one of these fell out of an animal like [[monsters/black_horse|that one]]; and she knows better than anybody at that fire what it is to put a stone into a piece of steel and then swing it every working day for the rest of your life. She has not explained herself. She is not going to.
gm_notes: The windowsill is the record: the missing shadow is disputable when it is an animal at dusk and undeniable when it is a stone on a plank in daylight, which is exactly what a stone can do that a meeting cannot. The horse's passing-on history and Sigrun's 'the horse hauls charcoal' belong to the creature record and are not repeated. Her refusal is new and she gives no reason; the reason is the hammer, alluded to and never named. She has never been shown declining work before — use sparingly.
